The $\varepsilon_i$ are independent with mean zero and $\varepsilon_i^2=1$. Let $i

e q$. If $\{p,q\}=\{i,j\}$, then $\varepsilon_i\varepsilon_j\varepsilon_p\varepsilon_q=1$. Otherwise one of $p,q$, say $p$, lies outside $\{i,j\}$; since also $p
e q$, the index $p$ occurs exactly once in the product, whose expectation is therefore zero. The pairs $(p,q)=(i,j)$ and $(p,q)=(j,i)$ contribute $o_{ij}^2\abs{\phi_i}^2\abs{\phi_j}^2$ and $o_{ij}o_{ji}(\phi_i\cdot\phi_j)^2=o_{ij}^2(\phi_i\cdot\phi_j)^2$, which gives the identity. The inequality follows from $(\phi_i\cdot\phi_j)^2\le\abs{\phi_i}^2\abs{\phi_j}^2$, $o_{ij}^2\le a^2$ and $\sum_{i
e j}\abs{\phi_i}^2\abs{\phi_j}^2\le(\sum_i\abs{\phi_i}^2)^2$.
